title: BCDU charge-discharge fault
body: If a Battery Charge/Discharge Unit reports persistent over-current trip during sunlit charge phase, the affected battery string is isolated within 60 s by autonomous logic. Manual override requires ground concurrence; the redundant string carries the bus through next eclipse.
citation: ISS Power Subsystem Spec SSP-30482; Operational Rules §3.2

title: Solar array shadowing during dock
body: When a visiting vehicle (Crew Dragon, Cygnus, Progress) approaches within 20 m, attitude must be biased to minimise shadowing of the active power channel. Power channel margin > 10 % must be maintained throughout the approach corridor.

title: ATCS loop ammonia leak
body: If External Active Thermal Control System (EATCS) loop pressure drop exceeds 10 psi/hour and not attributable to a commanded action, the leak procedure shall be invoked: isolate suspected segment, close affected QD, prepare loop-crossover.

title: Radiator panel attitude bias
body: ISS attitude shall be biased so that radiator panels see < 90 deg solar incidence during high-beta seasonal periods, otherwise heat rejection capability drops below margin and crew comfort/equipment limits are exceeded.

title: CMG saturation
body: If three of four Control Moment Gyros saturate, RCS thrusters shall augment torque authority. Saturation is allowed transient; persistent saturation > 10 minutes triggers desat burn or attitude bias to reduce environmental torques (gravity gradient + drag).

title: Microgravity jet selection during VV proximity
body: Within 200 m of any visiting vehicle, only fine-resolution RCS jets (low thrust ~10 N) may fire to avoid plume impingement on the VV. Coarse jets locked out by FCS logic.

title: Loss of S-band uplink
body: If S-band primary uplink lost > 5 minutes, switch to S-band redundant. If both lost > 30 minutes, fall back to UHF voice via SSPTS. Crew assumes loss-of-comm posture: no commanded actions without ground concurrence regained.

title: External ammonia leak detection + isolation
body: 1. Confirm leak via downstream pressure trending. 2. Isolate suspected QD/coldplate by closing manual valves per ICD. 3. Cross-feed surviving loop. 4. Reduce equipment load on affected coldplate. 5. Plan EVA repair if leak persists; use IFM kit for QD replacement.

title: EMU water leak detected during EVA
body: On detection of free water in EMU helmet (Parmitano 2013 incident), abort EVA immediately. Crewmate assists return to airlock. EMU repressurisation prioritises crew over fluid/scientific data.

title: Conjunction-avoidance burn threshold
body: If predicted miss distance < 2 km and probability of collision (Pc) > 1e-4, a Pre-Determined Debris Avoidance Maneuver (PDAM) shall be planned. Burn must be uplinked > 28.5 hours before TCA to allow tracking-data confirmation.
citation: JSC Conjunction Assessment Risk Analysis Process JSC-66050

title: Crew safe-haven configuration
body: Upon major depress / fire / toxic atmosphere event, crew retreat to designated safe haven (Soyuz or Crew Dragon) within the haven's allowable interior atmosphere. ISS hatches sealed; ground commanded power-down.
